summary: Resumed mid-diagnosis of the Slapdash session showing nothing after the user clarified they meant to steer, not abort. Reading Pi's `_queueSteer` to determine whether `agent.steer()` appends the user message to the session file — this determines if 'path' was a stranded steer against a provider-aborted run or a prompt whose run produced no output. Identified that `SessionOperations.abort()` never calls Pi's `clearQueue()`, leaving queued messages undelivered and not returned to the composer.
decisions: Interpret the user's correction ('i meant to steer') as invalidating the earlier 'user aborted to fix typo' reading of the transcript.
Read `_queueSteer` (agent-session.js:1046) to determine whether steer() persists the message to the session file before deciding between fix paths.
Treat the diagnosis as still open: confirm with the user before implementing the abort/clearQueue fix and any client-side surfacing of stranded steers.
errors: Prior wrong advice to 'reload the tab' for the stuck 'running' tool display — `sessionTranscript` rebuilds `status: 'running'` from the file every load, so reloads don't fix it.
Initial misreading of the Slapdash transcript as a deliberate abort to correct a typo, invalidated by the user's correction that they meant to steer.

Two aborts within ~53s across cronkis and Slapdash, both provider/model `opencode-go`/`glm-5.3-flash`, both 'Request was aborted' with zero usage — suggests a provider/network event rather than user action.
